title: Agentic Search vs Vector Search for Coding Agents: We Ran the Eval — Braintrust
talk_summary: Braintrust's devrel explains evals as dataset/task/scorer/experiment and runs a coding-agent eval comparing vector search vs agentic search on TypeScript-Go fix PRs. Agentic search matched accuracy at one-quarter the cost; vector chunks lacked imports/callers and caused more searches.

takeaways.what_they_do: Mine merged PRs titled 'fix', check out the parent commit with the bug, generate a bug task from the diff, run agents to locate/fix it, and score by the repo test suite.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we basically found all the PRs, the merged PRs with the title fix in them
takeaways.numbers: ~20 PRs; vector and agentic search had same accuracy; vector cost 4x more

takeaways.what_they_do: Give coding agents grep/find/ls/cat/bash so they follow function calls and read full files instead of relying on semantic chunks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vector search returns back chunks of code, but these chunks of code often miss things like imports or tool calls or the calling code above it
takeaways.numbers: vector agent made 26 searches and still could not piece together three functions across files

takeaways.technique: Hard-disable tools to isolate eval condition
takeaways.what_they_do: When testing vector search inside Claude Code, they explicitly disallow agentic-search tools via flags because prompt instructions alone do not reliably prevent tool use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: prompting is never enough. So, what we also had to do is use the disallowed tools flag

takeaways.technique: Parent span IDs for subprocess traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Run Claude Code as subprocesses but pass parent span IDs as environment variables so traces are not orphaned and every turn/tool call is visible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: passing the parent span IDs as environment variables

takeaways.what_they_do: They note the eval should run multiple trials per task because LLMs are nondeterministic and should expand beyond ~20 rows/repos.
takeaways.evidence_quote: running multiple trials per task, especially because LLMs are so non-deterministic

takeaways.technique: Cost per successful task as routing metric
takeaways.what_they_do: They compare accuracy and cost, finding vector search matched accuracy but cost 4x because it made more searches and LLM calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: vector search cost, uh, four times more than agentic search
